column15: Tomintoul distillery's peated single malt, released under its old spring-name "Ballantruan" rather than the Tomintoul brand name. Wiki: "a 1991 peaty vintage was released under the name 'Old Ballantruan'"..."it has released a peated single malt called Ballantruan". No phenol ppm figure found in the source; general reputation (and the fact it is marketed as Tomintoul's peat-forward counterpart) supports heavy over medium, but the exact figure is not confirmed -- confidence kept low rather than high.

No web presence found. Catalogue calls it "bourbon" but it is sold from Spain, an unusual combination -- left type/peat unknown rather than trust the bourbon guess. Similar unidentifiable own-label pattern to the existing "Jim Bardett" row from another batch (different spelling; not assumed to be the same producer).
No source found (single-product own label); treated as ordinary blended Scotch per category convention.
Generic name, no identifiable web presence found; single-product own label.
No web presence found; treated as an ordinary own-label blended Scotch per budget policy.

One of the oldest continuously produced American whiskey brands (since 1810), produced at Jim Beam's distillery. 'jim-beam' is a well-known distillery slug another batch will almost certainly emit -- not created here.

Van Winkle family's wheated-bourbon brand, distilled/bottled by Sazerac at Buffalo Trace under a joint venture since 2002. No explicit peat statement found (sources covered ownership/history, not tasting notes); inferred unpeated from standard bourbon mashbill

Single-barrel cask-strength Kentucky straight bourbon bottled by Augusta Distillery (Augusta, KY), the distillery's inaugural bourbon. Sourced from an undisclosed Kentucky distillery ('rumored' Heaven Hill, not confirmed) so no parentSlug given per the undisclosed-origin rule. No smoke/peat in tasting notes (oak-char notes only).
Not researched (budget); generic "Old ___'s" own-label naming, origin unconfirmed.

Blended Scotch (min. 25% malt content) evoking the historic Tullymet distillery (built 1812 as Auchnagie, renamed Tullymet 1890, long since closed) -- heritage branding, not a claim that the liquid comes from that site. No peat/smoke mentioned; described as smooth and elegant.
Single product, no information found this session, not searched (long tail budget)
Catalogue supplied no type/country guess; no web presence found. Own-label, origin unclear -- possibly an invented Irish-sounding name rather than genuinely Irish.

Rhetoric is an aged-bourbon release under the Orphan Barrel project; the specific source distillery/mashbill for this release was not confirmed this session so kept as kind=blend rather than naming a distillery. Standard bourbon category, no peat.
No web presence found. Unlike most of this batch's unidentified own labels, the name has no 'Glen'/Scottish styling, so it was left unclassified rather than defaulted to blended Scotch.
Brand not independently verified via any source actually opened (no hits found); American-themed name suggests US whiskey, category default (peat is a Scotch-specific practice) applied.

Originally created by Spencerfield Spirit Company; acquired by Ian Macleod Distillers with their purchase of Spencerfield Spirits in September 2016 (confirmed via Wikipedia). Listed among Ian Macleod's core blended-Scotch brands, explicitly contrasted there with their peated Smokehead single malt -- read as implicitly unpeated.

Jacopo Poli is a well-known Italian grappa/brandy house (Bassano del Grappa, Veneto); could not confirm this session whether "Segretario di Stato" is genuinely a whisky release of theirs or a mislabeled grappa/brandy product (poligrappa.com returned 404 / redirected to an Italian-only page with no whisky content found). Kept as a low/unknown-confidence row rather than skipped outright, since the catalogue explicitly classifies it "malt"/IT -- flagged for human review of whether this is whisky at all.

Single product 'Ley Seca' (Spanish for 'dry law' / Prohibition). No whiskey/whisky brand by this name found on Wikipedia; 'Ley Seca' itself only returns the generic Prohibition term and an unrelated song. Left fully unknown -- flag for human review of what this product actually is (category/country not even confirmed).

Heaven Hill Quality House Old Style White appears to be a bottling/export label of Heaven Hill's Old Style White product. defaultTypeName left empty (mashbill/style of "Old Style White" unclear from samples). Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.

column15: Not researched (budget). "Ragtime" + "Rye" is a strongly American-coded name; countryCode/defaultTypeName inferred from the name only. Peat left unknown per no-citation policy (American rye is conventionally unpeated but this was not verified for this specific brand).
Irish whiskey (triple-distilled grain + double-distilled malt blend), aged 10 years in ex-bourbon casks, bottled for the German band Rammstein. No peat reported (standard Irish blend style).
Part of the unresolved Japanese-styled budget cluster (see Shinobu); single product, no web presence found this session

Richmond, Virginia craft distillery; official site lists bourbon, rye and corn whiskey with no peat mention. defaultTypeName left empty since range spans multiple types. Peat=none per general American-whiskey category norm.
